summary: Poha (flattened rice) with toasted coconut and cashews: thick poha soaked about 3 minutes and drained, then cooked about 3 minutes with sauteed onion, ginger, mustard seed, garam masala and turmeric, finished with lime and served with lime pickle.
glance: 2 as a main dish or 4 as a side dish or part of a thali
yield: 2 as a main dish or 4 as a side dish or part of a thali
faq: What is poha?

Rice that has been flattened, popular in India and used in a whole range of dishes, often on thalis. It cooks very quickly, has a light, fluffy texture and is quite neutral in flavor, so it takes to many treatments.
Where do I find poha?
Not at a regular supermarket or Whole Foods. Look at an Indian grocer, or order it online. There are usually at least two thicknesses, and the author prefers thick poha, which is the most forgiving.
How do I keep poha from turning to mush?
Don't oversoak or overcook the flakes. Soak in water until fairly tender but not falling apart, about 3 minutes, then drain in a sieve before they fall apart, pressing lightly.
Do I have to use coconut?
No. If you don't care for coconut, leave it out and you'll still have a delicious dish.
What do I serve with poha?
Lime pickle on the side, plus cilantro. It also works as a side dish or part of a thali.

summary: Mujadara is a rice, lentil and caramelized onion pilaf spiked with cumin and cinnamon: 3 pounds of onions cooked about 65 minutes, folded with separately cooked brown or green lentils and rice and served with Greek yogurt; serves 4.
glance: Prep 20 min, cook 1 hr, total 1 hr 20 min
3 pounds, cooked about 45 minutes on medium-low, then 20+ minutes on medium-high
1 1/2 cups brown or green (not red or French)
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan with oil instead of butter
faq: What is mujadara?

A mixture of rice and perfectly cooked lentils, spiked with a big dose of caramelized onions and a bit of cumin and cinnamon. It is a delicious, inexpensive, simple dish, spelled several ways such as mujadarah or megadarra.
What lentils should I use?
Brown or green lentils, not red lentils or French lentils. Cook them separately and watch carefully: they should not be crunchy, but must keep their shape. This isn't lentil soup.
Why cook the rice and lentils separately?
Some people cook them together, but the author doesn't think that gives enough control over the texture.
How long do the onions take?

A good bit of time: about 45 minutes on medium-low until very soft, then 20 minutes or more on medium-high until deeply browned and sweet, then deglaze with wine, vermouth or water. Consider doubling the onions and freezing the extra.
What do you serve with mujadara?

It is a hearty one-dish meal with thick Greek yogurt and maybe a cucumber salad, or part of a larger Middle Eastern feast. It is really good at room temperature and gets better after a day in the refrigerator.
Is mujadara vegan?
It is vegetarian and gluten-free, and vegan if you use oil or margarine instead of butter and skip the yogurt.

summary: Persian baked zucchini: 2 pounds of zucchini tossed with olive oil, dried mint, dried dill and cayenne, covered and baked at 400°F for about 25 minutes, then topped with breadcrumbs and browned about 5 more minutes; finished with feta.
glance: 400°F: about 25 minutes covered, then about 5 minutes with breadcrumbs

Vegetarian; vegan without the feta; gluten-free without the breadcrumbs
faq: Why use dried mint in Persian cooking?

We normally think of dried mint only for tea, but in Persian cuisine it is frequently used in savory foods, where it adds a pleasing hint of bitterness and only a hint of actual mintiness. It is a completely different product from fresh mint, not a replacement.
How do you bake the zucchini?

Toss everything in a baking dish that holds the zucchini in a single layer, cover with foil and bake at 400°F until tender, about 25 minutes. Remove the foil, sprinkle on breadcrumbs and bake or carefully broil until browned, about 5 more minutes.
Can I make it vegan or gluten-free?
Omit the feta for vegan, and omit the breadcrumbs for gluten-free.
What do I serve with Persian baked zucchini?
It goes great with chickpea and potato stew, Persian rice pilaf (chelo with tahdig), or Syrian red lentil soup.
How do I serve it?
Hot or warm, garnished with crumbled feta and a little more olive oil drizzled on at the last moment.

glance: around 10 cups, easily serving 5 (doubles or triples beautifully)

Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you modify the garnishes
faq: How do you control the heat in vegetarian chili?

The sauce is flavored mainly with whole dried chiles, so control the spice by how many you use and how hot they are. Build a moderately spicy base, then add canned chipotle in adobo to taste near the end, and offer hot sauces on the side.
Can I leave out the chipotle if I don't like heat?
Don't omit it completely: it provides a lot of fruity flavor and thickens the sauce. Just use milder chiles such as ancho.
Do I need to soak the beans?

The author soaks them overnight, because overnight-soaked beans come out more tender and delicious, much better than canned. A quick soak starting with hot water for a couple of hours also works, but isn't the same.
Can I use fresh chiles?
No. Fresh chiles are for completely different types of dishes; use whole dried chiles such as ancho, guajillo, pasilla, cascabel or de arbol.
Can I make chili ahead or freeze it?
Yes. It gets better over the course of a couple of days and freezes well. You can make it on the weekend and eat it all week.
What goes on top?
Sliced green onion or minced white onion, cilantro, grated cheddar or queso anejo or cotija, sour cream or queso fresco, and lime wedges.
